source.title: Diversity-Aware Agnostic Ensemble of Sharpness Minimizers
source.authors: Anh-Vu Bui; Vy Vo; Tung Pham; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung Le

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether combining sharpness-aware training and diversity promotion improves ensemble test accuracy on image classification datasets; this is a new ensemble setting beyond the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ensemble test accuracy for several training methods and ablations. These results do not measure the mapped versions’ random-label memorization, width sweep, convolutional versus fully connected comparison, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness-gap relation, or memorized-example removal. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization rationale to develop DASH and reports ensemble performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against train–test gaps or compare generalization measures as V7 specifies. Its experiments also do not test V1–V6 or V8. A new ensemble method and setting alone do not establish a test of a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors argue that DASH's agnostic diversity term promotes divergence among base-classifier predictions and improves ensemble generalization. This is a conclusion about their training method, not a test of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–gap correlation.
record.recipe_differences: Trains ensembles with a proposed combination of sharpness-aware minimization and an agnostic diversity-aware constraint; evaluates ensemble accuracy rather than random-label memorization or a train-test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR100 with R10x5, accuracy varies with γ: 80.84 at γ = 0.1 and 78.86 at γ = 1.0. DASH's relative result also varies across dataset and ensemble architecture settings; on CIFAR10 RME, SAM is 93.4 while DASH is 92.6.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports higher DASH ensemble accuracy than SGD and SAM in every recorded setting. Correctly aligned CIFAR10 RME values are SGD 92.6%, SAM 93.8% and DASH 95.2%; the record's apparent exception is an extraction error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining sharpness-aware training with diversity promotion can improve image-classification ensemble test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: In Table 5, DASH improves accuracy over flat-seeking-only DASHF by 0.84 points on CIFAR10 and 2.44 points on CIFAR100. On CIFAR100 its LD score increases from -19.47 to -18.92, remaining below SGD's -16.88.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diversity promotion can improve prediction diversity and accuracy relative to flat-seeking-only ensemble training, without necessarily restoring SGD's diversity.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ensemble-accuracy table values. The adversarial robustness section explicitly uses a weaker attack than attacks commonly used to challenge defenses; those results do not measure the mapped versions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 Cal-Brier/uncertainty results, Tables 2–3, and adversarial-robustness figures were left out because they do not measure a mapped version or train-test gap. The remaining reported Table 1 ensemble-accuracy results and Table 5 accuracy/diversity ablation results are recorded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions and recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, underfitting and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps among comparably fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their accuracy and diversity values cannot establish any listed version, so cannot_determine replaces observed where necessary; this does not mean the reported performance is absent. Table 1's flattened RME columns caused several method/value misassignments, including the spurious claim that DASH underperforms SAM on CIFAR10. Table 1 and Table 5 also report different RME accuracy values; preserve their separate locators rather than merging them. No omitted result in the supplied text directly tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch training and epoch-budget effects.
Dropout effects and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measured against train-test gaps and comparison with other measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
